## Context
Gerrit Verify run 31892203411 completed in 31m59s; macOS remained the critical path, with the default pytest step taking 1,545.29s and integration 155.01s. The shared `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` runs the same default selector in Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13 for both the Gerrit Verified lane and the `test.yml` branch/PR lane, even for tests whose only input is the immutable checked-out repository tree. A node-level audit identified the exact 19 repository-policy/AST cases below. They passed locally under three workers in 8.28s: an expected macOS reduction of about 8 seconds (0.54% of the sampled 1,545.29s default step) and about 24.84 aggregate runner-seconds removed across the three duplicate cells in the same local environment. This is modest critical-path and runner-contention hygiene, not a standalone cure for a 32-minute run.

Moving whole files or general behavioral tests would weaken macOS platform coverage; adding a new Ubuntu shard would duplicate checkout, install, collection, and session fixtures and consume another contentious runner. Five surveyed active OSS projects (pytest, pip, Pydantic, Click, uv) keep behavioral suites on macOS and run static/lint checks on Linux. Internal precedents feathered-ironclad-macaque and isleless-catatonic-ekaltadeta accept singleton routing; ropeable-hydrated-siskin and coercive-paediatric-bug reject reduced macOS behavioral coverage and extra runner sharding.

## Plan
- Register a strict `repo_policy` pytest marker for tests whose complete contract is an OS/Python-invariant scan of repository text or AST.
- Mark exactly the inventory above at node/function level, not whole mixed modules. Retain runtime, subprocess, filesystem, locking, timeout, and Git behavior in all four cells.
- In the existing shared default-suite process, keep marked nodes on Ubuntu 3.13 and append `and not repo_policy` only for Ubuntu 3.11, Ubuntu 3.12, and macOS 3.13. The shared reusable applies identically to the Gerrit and branch/PR callers. Add no job or pytest session.
- Extend `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`; reuse `_collect_node_ids` and `_expanded_test_matrix` rather than creating a parallel oracle. Collect the real selectors, pin the exact marker inventory, prove the primary/non-primary partition, prove unmarked nodes in the mixed modules retain their original selection, and prove integration routing remains unchanged.
- Preserve the coverage report on Ubuntu 3.13 and every existing default/integration matrix cell.
- Run focused tests, workflow parity, lint, typecheck, and the complete non-external suite. Back out with a Gerrit revert if collection multiplicity or platform coverage regresses.
- After merge, record the next organic full-route timing on the parent RCA ticket as a non-blocking observation; do not create a control-only run and do not gate this child close on an unscheduled external event.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exactly the 19 inventoried cases carry the strict marker.
- [ ] Every marked assertion collects in the Ubuntu 3.13 default selection.
- [ ] Every marked assertion is absent from each non-primary default selection.
- [ ] Every unmarked case in the seven mixed modules retains its prior default selection.
- [ ] Runtime and subprocess cases in the seven mixed modules remain unmarked.
- [ ] The integration selector is unchanged.
- [ ] All four default/integration matrix cells remain present.
- [ ] No new CI job or runner is added.
- [ ] No checkout, dependency-install, collection, or fixture session is added.
- [ ] The existing workflow-parity test surface contains the routing oracle.
- [ ] Focused repository-policy tests pass.
- [ ] Workflow-parity tests pass.
- [ ] Lint passes.
- [ ] Typecheck passes.
- [ ] The complete non-external suite passes.
- [ ] Gerrit records LLM-Review +1 before merge.
- [ ] Gerrit records Verified +1 before merge.
